name: Malpractice cover, claims, and patient-safety incidents
one_line: The organizational situation of something having gone wrong, or being alleged to have gone wrong, in the holder's clinical care - and of the professional indemnity cover that stands behind it. It runs from an internal incident report through a complaint, a duty-of-candour letter, an investigation, an expert report, a claim, and an indemnity or regulatory outcome. It is a THREE-schema world by nature (clinical, legal, finance) and this row's job is to recognize and protect it, not to adjudicate it. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND); it writes NO field rows, because the clinical_practice schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence, and specifically never a licence to conclude that anything went wrong. This template's schema declares no field rows. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

an incident-report structure: a labelled incident-reference slot beside a date-and-time-of-incident slot, a location or service slot, a category or severity designation copied from the reporting system's own vocabulary, and a free-text account. The severity designation is a RAW OBSERVATION from a source system and never becomes this product's sensitivity classification.
a complaint-handling structure: a complainant block, an acknowledgement or response-deadline slot, a chronology of the care complained of, and a formal response letter naming a responsible officer.
a duty-of-candour or open-disclosure letter structure: an addressee who is the patient or a relative, an account of what happened, an apology section, and a record of what was offered.

an indemnity or professional-liability policy structure: a medical defence organisation or insurer letterhead, a labelled policy-number slot, a cover-period slot, a premium amount, and a scope-of-practice or specialty line.

a claim structure: a claim or reference identifier beside an instructing-solicitor or claims-handler block, a letter-of-claim or notification designation, and a reserve or settlement figure. This is the evidence item finance and legal read equally well, so it resolves per-item under CONNECTION section 4 step 3.
a medico-legal report structure: an instructing party, a statement of the expert's duty, an itemised review of records, an opinion section, and a declaration and signature block.
a regulatory or disciplinary structure: a health regulator or facility investigation office as sender, a case reference, an allegation summary, and a response deadline.

an archive whose manifest names an incident, claim, or investigation bundle with member paths partitioned by document kind, read from the manifest alone - “the normal scan should never extract archive contents to the filesystem”.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: this material concerns a named patient AND exposes the holder personally, so a model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” The exposure here is two-sided, which is stated as inference and is not a 00 claim.
separating a real incident record from a training scenario, a simulation debrief, a policy example, or an audit case sample that reproduces the reporting form exactly.

separating an incident that concerns the HOLDER's care from one the holder merely investigated, witnessed, or received as departmental circulation. The model must abstain rather than assert: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
an unstructured account - a personal reflective note, a contemporaneous aide-memoire, an email chain with no form and no reference.

a purpose-coherent claim bundle whose members are individually unremarkable: records, statements, a policy schedule, correspondence, an invoice. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
never_alone: incident, complaint, claim, negligence, error, harm, or apology vocabulary alone. Policies, training material, guidance, journal articles, and consumer correspondence all use it, and this is the tempting false file for this row.
a reference-shaped token alone, and a bare 4-digit number read as an incident year, a claim number, or a policy year.

an insurer, defence organisation, regulator, or law-firm gazetteer hit alone, read across from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” by inference - the same name appears as underwriter, member-benefit publisher, conference host, and correspondent.
a source system's own severity, harm, or risk designation as this product's sensitivity classification. It is a raw observation and nothing more.

any inference of fault, causation, breach, liability, privilege, or admissibility. The product records literal observations and abstains - “Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement.”
source_type or extension alone. 00: “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a parent folder named Incidents, Complaints, or Claims alone.
membership in a download session that dropped a bundle's attachments at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”

grouping_reasons: one incident from first report to closure, across reports, statements, investigation, correspondence, and outcome. The anchor supports a candidate packet; it never writes a subject, a cause, or a fault fact onto members - “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
one claim, joined by an exact claim or reference identifier rather than by similar filenames.
one indemnity period across its schedule, certificate, invoice, and renewal.
one disclosure or production set, joined by a production or bundle index.
no group at all is a valid outcome; a single stray statement is still protected material on both counts.

template.why: Empty by binding contract and by an unusually strong privacy argument. By contract: clinical_practice declares no fields, so no dimension can branch (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, PR-6). By privacy: a folder whose LABEL names an incident, a claim, or a patient discloses, from the namespace alone and without any file being opened, that an allegation exists - about a named third party's care and about the holder personally. That is disclosure by structure, and it is the one place on this roster where the folder name is more dangerous than the folder contents. “Protected branches should have configurable redaction in the canvas and review screens” and “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.” both point the same way. The present recommendation is ONE shallow, redacted, user-approved packet with no automatic internal depth and no label derived from the matter. Held as prose: if fields ever land, the professional situation would precede document function, and neither a patient level nor an outcome level would ever be proposed. Not time-first - “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.”.

collides_with.signal: A claim against the holder is a legal matter in which the holder is a party, and the same letters, bundles, and expert reports appear on both sides. The discriminating evidence: a clinical-care account, an incident-reporting-system reference, an indemnity policy, or a duty-of-candour letter supports this row; a tribunal caption or a matter anchored outside clinical care supports the legal row. A law-firm letterhead and a claim reference support both equally, which is what the mutex is for. Provenance: inference.

Structurally identical documents, opposite roles. The discriminating evidence is who the holder is: a defendant clinician whose care is in question supports this row; a practitioner acting FOR a client, evidenced by a signed engagement record, a firm matter-system identifier, or counsel work product, supports the law-practice row. An expert report, a disclosure bundle, and a letter of claim appear in both corpora unchanged. Provenance: inference.

A professional indemnity schedule reads exactly like any other liability policy: insurer, policy number, cover period, premium. The discriminating evidence: a scope-of-clinical-practice or specialty line, a medical defence organisation, or an attached claims history about patient care leans here; a general business or property liability policy is the finance template's. The pair also holds on disjoint evidence (PR-8), so this signal exists to stop one policy-shaped item counting twice. Provenance: inference.

Morbidity-and-mortality and significant-event reviews carry both anchors. The discriminating evidence: an incident reference, a formal reporting form, a complaint, or claims correspondence supports this row; a recurring meeting series with attendance and a multi-case agenda supports the case-conference row. Provenance: inference.

An incident-reporting policy and a safety alert are ABOUT incidents without being one. The discriminating evidence: a real reference, a real subject, or a real account supports this row; a version token, a review date, an approval committee, and a worked example support the guideline row. Incident vocabulary alone supports neither. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The primary home for a recognised incident, complaint, claim, statement, or bundle when no accepted group or approved branch exists - and the home whose local-only rule matters most on this row. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The cautious outcome for a document that reads as an account of something going wrong but whose reference, party, and role are unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The safe outcome for a password-protected disclosure bundle, an unreadable claims export, or an untranscribed recording. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

The home for a standalone indemnity certificate or policy schedule with no incident around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The home for an isolated premium invoice or payment confirmation. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

The inactive home for safety policies, alerts, and articles about incidents with no case attached. “Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.”

sensitivity_why: The exposure runs in two directions at once, which is unusual on this roster and is stated as inference rather than as a 00 claim: the material concerns a named patient's care AND it concerns an allegation against the holder, so a leak harms someone who is not the user and someone who is. 00 names both kinds of material in one corpus list - “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and requires the immediate transition: “A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately.”. The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class, and it makes no finding about privilege, admissibility, disclosure, or fault - those are outside this product's vocabulary entirely.
open_question: Two. (1) Whether an incident or claim packet may be MOVED at all, even inside a frozen tree - moving a claim bundle changes paths that other people's processes may depend on, and the mere existence of a differently-named branch is itself a disclosure. The other placeholder rows defer their tree to a field decision; this one has a reason to prefer represent-in-place permanently, and that is Joseph's call. (2) The boundary against legal.practice-matter-file when the holder is BOTH clinician and instructing party - a clinician-director of a practice receiving a claim about a colleague's care. The evidence supports both rows and the roster currently gives no rule for it; R1c should decide whether this needs a reciprocal edge on the legal side or whether it is simply an unresolved-outcome case.
